title: Why your fetch() call ignores a 404
description:
One of the most common JavaScript networking bugs: fetch() does not throw on HTTP errors. A 404 or 500 response still resolves successfully, so a missing check silently passes broken data downstream. This Short shows the gotcha and the one-line fix using response.ok.

Source lesson(s):
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/javascript-mastery-path/level-2/05-json-fetch/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Your fetch call finishes with no error. The server actually sent back a 404. And your code has no idea anything went wrong.
Here's the trap. Fetch returns a promise, and that promise only rejects on a network failure, like a dead connection or a bad DNS lookup.
A 404 or a 500 still resolves like a success. So you check it yourself. If response dot ok is false, throw, and let your catch block handle it.
Response dot ok is true only for status codes in the two hundreds. Make that check a habit on every fetch you write.
